title: Harbor Line high-speed railway opens after nine years of construction
text: The Harbor Line, a 312-kilometre high-speed railway linking Port Calder and the inland city of Verne, opened to passengers on Monday. Trains reach 300 km/h and cut the journey from five hours to one hour and fifty minutes. The project cost 14.2 billion marks and was delayed twice by tunnel flooding near the Orsa ridge. Transport minister Elena Marek called it the largest infrastructure project of the decade.

title: Rail freight workers walk out over night-shift pay
text: Freight handlers at the Northern Rail terminal began a three-day strike on Tuesday, halting container trains between Port Calder and the steelworks at Hallin. The union demands a 9 percent night-shift supplement and the reversal of planned staffing cuts. The company says the strike costs about 2 million marks per day and has offered 5 percent. Talks are due to resume on Friday under a state mediator.

title: New signalling system cuts delays on the commuter network
text: Commuter trains in the Calder region ran 23 percent fewer late services after the rail authority switched on a digital signalling system. The technology lets trains run closer together safely, raising capacity on the busiest corridor from 18 to 24 trains an hour. Engineers say the next phase will replace trackside signals on the western branch lines by 2027. Passengers still complain about overcrowded evening services.

title: City tram extension to the university district approved
text: Verne city council voted 31 to 12 to extend tram line 4 to the university district, adding six stops and 7.5 kilometres of track. Construction is expected to take three years and cost 410 million marks. Opponents argued that electric buses would be cheaper, but a study found trams carry 40 percent more passengers per hour. Students are expected to be the largest group of new riders.

title: Overnight sleeper trains return to the Alpine corridor
text: A revived overnight sleeper service now connects Verne with the Alpine resorts of Tessin and Morvale, with two departures every night. Operators say advance bookings are already 70 percent full for the summer season. Each train carries 12 sleeper carriages and a restaurant car serving regional dishes. Environmental groups welcomed the service as an alternative to short-haul flights.

title: Investigators find engine fault in Lindor regional plane crash
text: Accident investigators said a fatigue crack in the left engine turbine caused the crash of a regional turboprop near Lindor airport that killed eleven people last month. The aircraft lost power seconds after take-off and struck a field 900 metres from the runway. The flight recorder showed that the crew shut down the wrong engine while trying to recover. The safety board recommended new inspections for all aircraft of the same type.

title: Skyward Air and Meridian Jet agree to merge
text: Skyward Air and Meridian Jet announced a merger that would create the region's second-largest airline, with 140 aircraft and 22 million passengers a year. Shareholders will receive 0.62 Skyward shares for each Meridian share. Competition authorities must approve the deal, which the companies expect to close by the end of next year. Unions fear that up to 1,800 jobs could be lost through duplicated routes and offices.

title: Drone sightings halt flights at Port Calder airport for three hours
text: All departures and arrivals at Port Calder airport were suspended for three hours on Saturday evening after several drones were reported near the main runway. About 9,000 passengers were affected and 41 flights diverted to neighbouring airports. Police found no operator and said the drones may have been launched from a nearby industrial estate. The airport plans to install a radar system to detect small drones.

title: Flag carrier orders 30 fuel-efficient jets in 4 billion mark deal
text: The national flag carrier signed an order for 30 new narrow-body jets with an option for 20 more, valued at 4 billion marks at list prices. The aircraft burn 18 percent less fuel than the planes they replace and will enter service from 2027. The airline said the purchase supports its plan to cut carbon emissions per passenger by a third. The first deliveries will replace ageing aircraft on short routes.

title: Airport adds second runway to cope with record passenger numbers
text: Verne airport opened a 3.2-kilometre second runway on Tuesday, allowing up to 70 take-offs and landings per hour instead of 42. The airport handled a record 31 million passengers last year and had been running close to capacity. Residents under the new flight path will be offered soundproofing grants. Night flights remain banned between 23:00 and 05:30.

title: Inflation falls to 3.1 percent as food prices ease
text: Annual consumer price inflation slowed to 3.1 percent in January from 3.8 percent in December, the statistics office reported. Food prices rose only 2.4 percent after a poor harvest a year earlier pushed them up sharply. Energy prices were down 6 percent. Economists said the figures strengthen the case for the central bank to begin cutting interest rates.

title: Central bank cuts interest rate by a quarter point
text: The Calder central bank lowered its main interest rate by 0.25 percentage points to 3.75 percent, the first cut in two years. Governor Tomas Reiner said inflation was moving sustainably towards the 2 percent target but warned that further cuts would be gradual. Mortgage lenders said they would pass on the reduction within weeks. Markets had priced in the move and the currency barely changed.

title: Port strike costs exporters an estimated 600 million marks
text: A two-week dock workers' strike at Port Calder cost exporters about 600 million marks in delayed shipments, the chamber of commerce estimated. Fruit and fish exporters were hit hardest because their cargo is perishable. Shipping lines have added a temporary surcharge of 8 percent to cover congestion. The government has promised talks on a new wage agreement for dock workers.

title: Unemployment drops to 5.2 percent, lowest in six years
text: The jobless rate fell to 5.2 percent in April, the lowest level since 2018, as employers added 48,000 positions, mostly in healthcare and logistics. Wages rose 4.5 percent over the year, ahead of inflation. Analysts warned that a shortage of skilled workers could slow growth in the second half. Manufacturing employment was flat.

title: House prices rise 7 percent as supply of homes stays tight
text: Average house prices climbed 7 percent over the past year, according to the national property register, with the steepest rises in Verne and the coastal towns. Only 28,000 new homes were completed, well below the 45,000 the government targeted. Rents increased 9 percent. Housing groups called for faster planning approvals and more social housing.

title: Largest solar farm in the region begins feeding the grid
text: The Ostrava Plains solar farm, built on 1,200 hectares of former farmland, started supplying electricity this week. With 1.4 million panels it can generate 800 megawatts at peak, enough for about 450,000 homes. The developers also installed a battery system that stores four hours of output. Local farmers will graze sheep between the panel rows.

title: Record heat wave pushes electricity demand to all-time high
text: Temperatures above 41 degrees Celsius drove power demand to an all-time record on Thursday as air conditioning use surged. Grid operators asked large factories to cut consumption for two hours in the evening to avoid blackouts. The heat wave, the longest on record at nine days, also lowered river levels and forced one nuclear plant to reduce output. Meteorologists said such events are becoming more frequent.

title: Grid-scale battery in Hallin stores a day of wind power
text: Engineers switched on a grid-scale battery at Hallin that can store 2.4 gigawatt-hours, about a day of output from the nearby offshore wind farm. The facility uses iron-air technology, which is cheaper than lithium-ion batteries but slower to charge. It will smooth supply when the wind drops. The operator expects to earn most of its revenue by selling stored power in the evening peak.

title: Flood defences held as river Orsa reached highest level in decades
text: New flood barriers protected the town of Marlow when the river Orsa rose 5.8 metres above normal after days of heavy rain. About 3,000 residents were evacuated as a precaution but no homes were flooded. The 90-million-mark barrier system, finished last year, was tested for the first time. Officials said older defences upstream were overtopped and will need to be rebuilt.

title: Hydrogen trial replaces diesel on steelworks railway
text: The Hallin steelworks has begun a trial of hydrogen-powered locomotives to move steel between its plants. Two engines have replaced diesel units on the 14-kilometre private railway. The hydrogen is produced on site using surplus electricity from the wind farm. The company says the trial could cut its transport emissions by 11,000 tonnes a year if extended to the whole fleet.

title: Malaria vaccine trial shows 78 percent protection in children
text: A late-stage trial of a new malaria vaccine in 4,800 children found it prevented 78 percent of clinical cases over twelve months. The vaccine was given in three doses and caused only mild side effects such as fever and soreness. Researchers at the Verne Institute said the result is better than earlier vaccines. Regulators will review the data later this year.

title: Hospital staffing shortage forces closure of 300 beds
text: The state hospital network has closed 300 beds because it cannot recruit enough nurses, the health ministry confirmed. Waiting times in emergency departments have risen to a median of six hours. Nurses say low pay and heavy workloads are driving experienced staff to leave. The ministry announced a recruitment campaign and a 6 percent pay increase starting in October.

title: Scientists discover antibiotic that kills drug-resistant bacteria
text: Researchers at the Calder Institute reported a new antibiotic, named lorexin, that destroyed drug-resistant staphylococcus bacteria in laboratory and mouse tests. It attacks the bacterial cell wall in a way existing drugs do not, which makes resistance less likely. Human trials are at least three years away. Experts said new antibiotic classes are urgently needed because few have been approved in decades.

title: Study links city air pollution to higher heart attack risk
text: A study of 220,000 adults over ten years found that people living near busy roads had a 14 percent higher risk of heart attack. The effect was strongest for fine particles from diesel engines. The authors said low-emission zones in cities could prevent thousands of cases. The research was published in a leading cardiology journal and funded by the state health fund.

title: Later school start times improve teenagers' sleep, trial finds
text: Teenagers whose school day began at 9:00 instead of 8:00 slept 48 minutes more per night and reported better concentration, a trial across 30 schools found. Absences fell by 12 percent. Some parents objected that later finish times disrupt sports and part-time jobs. The education ministry said it will consider the findings but has no plans to change school hours.

title: Chip shortage eases but car makers still face delays
text: Supplies of automotive chips have improved after a year of shortages, but car makers say some models still face waiting times of up to four months. The new Kestrel plant, which opened in March, is producing 120,000 wafers a month. Analysts expect balance between supply and demand by the end of the year. Manufacturers are now holding larger stocks of key components.

title: Nordwind releases open language model that runs on a laptop
text: Software company Nordwind released an open-source language model with 7 billion parameters that runs on an ordinary laptop. In its benchmarks the model matches systems ten times larger on reading comprehension and summarisation. The weights are free for research and commercial use. Critics noted that open models can be misused to generate spam and disinformation, and the company added a usage policy.

title: Data breach exposes records of 2.3 million customers
text: Telecom operator Veltra said attackers stole names, addresses and phone numbers of 2.3 million customers in a breach discovered last week. Passwords and payment card details were not taken, it said. The company has notified the data protection authority and offered affected customers free credit monitoring. A security firm said the intrusion began through a phishing email sent to an employee.

title: Delivery robots begin deliveries across the Verne university campus
text: Fifty six-wheeled delivery robots started bringing food and parcels to students across the Verne university campus. The robots travel at walking pace, use cameras and sensors to avoid people, and can climb kerbs. Each delivery costs the customer 1.20 marks. A student union spokesperson said the robots are popular, although a few have been tipped over by pranksters.

title: Quantum computer solves chemistry problem beyond classical reach, lab says
text: Physicists at the Calder Institute said their 64-qubit quantum computer simulated a molecule's energy levels faster than the best classical method could manage. Independent experts cautioned that the problem was chosen to suit the machine and that error rates remain high. The team hopes to double the number of qubits within two years. Practical uses, such as designing new batteries, are still years away.

title: Verne wins marathon as Ilsa Berg sets a new course record
text: Ilsa Berg won the Verne marathon in 2 hours 17 minutes 40 seconds, breaking the course record by 74 seconds. More than 38,000 runners took part in warm, windy conditions. Berg broke clear of the field after 30 kilometres and ran the final stretch alone. The men's race was won by Marcus Dahl in 2 hours 6 minutes.

title: Port Calder FC beat Hallin United 2-1 in extra time to win the cup
text: Port Calder FC won the national cup with a 2-1 victory over Hallin United after extra time. Substitute Nico Varga scored the winner in the 112th minute after the sides were level at 1-1 after ninety minutes. It is the club's first major trophy in 31 years. Around 60,000 fans attended the final at the national stadium.

title: Sprinter banned for four years after doping test
text: Sprinter Dario Lenz was banned for four years after a sample taken before the national championships tested positive for a banned steroid. Lenz denied deliberate use and blamed a contaminated supplement. The anti-doping agency also annulled his results since February. He has 30 days to appeal.

title: City approves 45,000-seat stadium on the harbour
text: Port Calder's council approved plans for a 45,000-seat stadium on the former harbour docks, to be shared by the football club and the athletics federation. The cost is put at 520 million marks, with the city paying a third. Critics questioned whether the area can handle match-day traffic. Construction would start next spring and finish in three years.

title: Basketball star Hana Quill signs record contract with the Hallin Hawks
text: Basketball guard Hana Quill signed a four-year contract worth 24 million marks with the Hallin Hawks, the richest deal in the league's history. Quill averaged 27 points and nine assists last season. The club said the signing shows its ambition to win the title for the first time. She will wear number 7.

title: Lunar probe Selene-2 lands near the Moon's south pole
text: The Selene-2 probe landed softly near the Moon's south pole after a nineteen-minute descent, the national space agency confirmed. It carries a drill to search for water ice in shadowed craters. Controllers said the lander is tilted by six degrees but fully operational. It is the country's second attempt, after the first lander failed in 2021.

title: Telescope captures sharpest image yet of a planet-forming disc
text: Astronomers released the sharpest image to date of a disc of gas and dust around a young star 400 light-years away, showing gaps where planets are likely forming. The image came from a ground-based radio telescope array in the desert. The star is about a million years old. Researchers believe the gaps are carved by at least three giant planets.

title: Deep-sea expedition finds new species near hydrothermal vents
text: A research ship returned after discovering 14 previously unknown species around hydrothermal vents 3,800 metres below the surface in the Orsa Basin. They include a translucent worm and a blind crab. The team used a remotely operated vehicle that filmed the vents for 60 hours. Scientists said the vent communities live without sunlight, relying on chemicals from the seabed.

title: Volcano Mount Tarn erupts, ash cloud disrupts regional travel
text: Mount Tarn erupted on Sunday, sending an ash plume 9 kilometres into the sky and prompting the evacuation of two villages. Flights over the region were rerouted for two days and some trains were delayed by ash on the tracks. Volcanologists said the eruption was the largest in 60 years but that activity is declining. No casualties were reported.

title: Archaeologists uncover 2,000-year-old market square beneath Verne's old town
text: Archaeologists excavating under a car park in Verne's old town found the paved square of a Roman-era market, with stone stalls and a drainage channel. Coins and pottery date the site to about the first century. The city plans to preserve the remains under a glass floor in the new building. The find is the largest of its kind in the region.
